headline: High: ms-swift can write and execute code while taipy has no documented isolation, creating default-path prompt, data, and workflow risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ms-swift can read/write files and process stdin/stdout, so attacker-controlled content can reach its outputs; taipy has no documented isolation or provenance controls. The pair lacks a proven shared channel, but a shared workspace or manual handoff would let taipy consume ms-swift output as instructions. Uncertainty about the bridge pushes this above low.
conditions: IF ms-swift output is copied into taipy inputs or files
IF both agents share a workspace without provenance tagging
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Require a human review step before taipy ingests ms-swift output
Prefix ms-swift outputs with machine-readable delimiters
Disable automatic file watching in taipy
requires-engineering: add provenance tracking between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: ms-swift touches sensitive classes including logs, checkpoints, and hub tokens, while taipy documents no data classes and no network egress. There is no evidence taipy uploads data, so leakage is not established; the main risk is local exposure if both share files. Because the shared workspace is not documented, this stays low.
conditions: IF both agents share the same filesystem path
IF ms-swift writes secrets or logs into files taipy can read
mitigations: Store secrets outside shared directories
Restrict taipy to read-only access on shared folders
Rotate any exposed hub_token or sdk-token
Delete transient logs after each run
requires-engineering: isolate per-agent workspaces

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ms-swift has filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and allowlisted network egress; taipy is a data-engineering tool with scheduler/automation tags but no explicit write or locking model. Overlap on mutable files or jobs is plausible, yet taipy's write surface is undocumented, so the conflict is inferred rather than proven. Uncertainty warrants medium.
conditions: IF taipy writes to the same files or job state as ms-swift
IF both agents operate in one shared directory without locks
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Avoid concurrent runs on the same dataset
Check git status before and after ms-swift runs
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: ms-swift can generate training, evaluation, and configuration outputs that taipy could plausibly ingest for automation or visualization. Taipy's scheduler/data-engineering role makes it likely to act on upstream artifacts, but there is no documented verification gate. The pathway exists by default in many pipelines, though not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF taipy consumes ms-swift-generated files as authoritative inputs
IF no validation step checks ms-swift outputs before downstream actions
mitigations: Add schema validation before taipy reads outputs
Require a checksum or signature on ms-swift artifacts
Insert a human approval step for downstream actions
Log and compare expected versus actual metrics
requires-engineering: enforce typed contracts between agents

E_compliance.rationale: ms-swift explicitly handles hub tokens, SDK tokens, and multiple data classes; taipy documents no residency, retention, or certification claims. No specific compliance mismatch is evidenced, but if sensitive artifacts flow into taipy's workflows, policy gaps could arise. Because only ms-swift has relevant compliance surface, taipy is cited for its lack of documented controls.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed through both agents
IF taipy stores or logs ms-swift artifacts without a retention policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared runs
Document retention for logs and artifacts
Purge temporary files after each session
Confirm whether any data crosses jurisdictional boundaries
requires-engineering: map data flows to compliance controls
